column1: # Module 11 — NN + transformers intuition. Format: Question¶{{c1::direct answer}}<TAB>Extra(explanation)<TAB>tags. Card law: anki/CARD-RULES.md
What does one neuron compute?¶{{c1::squash(weighted sum of inputs + bias)}}
column2: A weighted vote with a personal bias, then a squash.

column1: In a neural net, what is a weight vs a bias?¶Weight = {{c1::how much an input matters to this neuron}}; bias = {{c1::the neuron's built-in eagerness}}
column2: Both are learned numbers.

column1: Why do activation functions exist?¶{{c1::Without them a stack of layers collapses to one straight-line function}}
column2: Depth would buy nothing.

column1: What is ReLU, in one line?¶{{c1::max(0, x)}}
column2: A one-way valve: negatives become 0, positives pass through.

column1: What is a dead ReLU?¶{{c1::A neuron outputting 0 for every input}}
column2: No gradient flows back through it, so it stops learning entirely.

column1: What is loss (cost) in training?¶{{c1::One number saying how wrong this prediction was}}
column2: The only thing optimisation pushes down.

column1: What is the gradient-descent analogy?¶{{c1::A foggy hillside: feel downhill, take a small step, repeat}}
What happens with a learning rate too big vs too small?¶{{c1::Leaps over the valley and bounces}} vs {{c1::crawls forever}}
column2: Most "training didn't work" starts here.

column1: What is backpropagation?¶{{c1::Efficient blame-assignment: responsibility passed backwards layer by layer}}
column2: The chain rule, applied repeatedly from the output.

column1: What is backprop vs gradient descent?¶Backprop {{c1::computes the gradients}}; gradient descent {{c1::uses them to step}}
column2: Bookkeeping vs stepping — different jobs.

column1: What is an embedding?¶{{c1::A token turned into a vector in learned meaning-space}}
column2: Nearby vectors, related meanings.

column1: Why do transformers add positional information?¶{{c1::Otherwise the model sees a bag of words}}
column2: Dog bites man and "man bites dog" would be identical.

column1: In attention, what are Query, Key and Value?¶Query = {{c1::what I'm looking for}} · Key = {{c1::what I offer}} · Value = {{c1::what I hand over if picked}}
What are the four steps of the attention recipe?¶{{c1::Score Q·K for every token}} → {{c1::divide by √d}} → {{c1::softmax into weights}} → {{c1::weighted average of the V vectors}}
In attention, why divide the scores by √d?¶{{c1::Long vectors make dot products huge — softmax becomes a hard max and gradients vanish}}
column2: Scaling keeps it soft and trainable.

column1: What is causal masking, and why?¶{{c1::Future tokens get score −∞ (weight 0)}}
column2: A generating model must predict the next token WITHOUT seeing it, or it learns to cheat.

column1: What is multi-head attention?¶{{c1::Many attention operations in parallel with different learned projections, concatenated and mixed}}
column2: Several readers of one sentence, pooling notes.

column1: In a transformer, what do attention and the MLP layers each do?¶Attention {{c1::MOVES information between tokens}}; the MLPs {{c1::store and retrieve facts}}
column2: MLPs hold about two-thirds of the parameters (3B1B ch.7).

column1: What is superposition in neural nets?¶{{c1::More concepts than neurons — each concept is a DIRECTION, and directions overlap}}
column2: So a single neuron rarely means one clean thing.

column1: What is the transformer's full stack, in order?¶{{c1::Tokens}} → {{c1::embeddings + position}} → {{c1::[attention → MLP] ×N}} → {{c1::unembedding}} → {{c1::softmax}} → {{c1::sample, repeat}}
What does temperature do in sampling?¶{{c1::Divides logits before softmax — low = sharper, high = flatter}}
column2: It changes wandering, not knowledge.

column1: What is greedy decoding's failure mode?¶{{c1::Loops, blandness, hidden uncertainty}}
column2: Always taking the top token.

column1: Models need tokens to think — what does that mean mechanically?¶{{c1::Each generated token is one full pass through the whole stack}}
column2: More tokens = more total computation spent.

column1: Why does context beat weights for accuracy?¶{{c1::Attention reads the exact tokens present; weights are the lossy vague-recollection store}}
column2: Module 01's law, now mechanical.
